themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints in East Harlem spiked to 43 THIS WEEK versus a 10.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 295% increase (z-score: 6.35)—coinciding with damaged street signs jumping 700% (3 complaints this week vs 0.4 avg). This acute infrastructure deterioration demands immediate investigation into root causes and repair timelines.
evidence: 43 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 10.9 weekly baseline (295% spike, z-score: 6.35)
3 damaged street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Community Board has repeatedly requested DOT funding for street lights and access improvements—unmet need over multiple budget cycles
reporting_angles: On-the-ground survey: which streets are deteriorating and why? Interview DOT about repair backlog.
Connect to Second Ave subway construction (mentioned in recent MTA news)—is construction activity accelerating street damage?

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage & Environmental Degradation
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints exploded to 4 LAST WEEK versus a 0.1 weekly average—a 3100% spike (z-score: 11.72), the most severe statistical anomaly in the dataset. This coincides with damaged tree complaints up 860% (12 complaints 3 weeks ago) and air quality complaints up 269% last week, suggesting a coordinated environmental crisis in the district.
evidence: 4 illegal tree damage complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (3100% spike, z-score: 11.72—highest severity in dataset)
12 damaged tree complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly average (860% spike, z-score: 4.84)
6 air quality complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average (269% spike, z-score: 4.41)
Community Board budget requests include DEP capital improvements—longstanding environmental investment gap
reporting_angles: Investigation: What triggered the tree damage spike? Construction, storm damage, or illegal removal?
Environmental justice angle: Is air quality degradation linked to tree loss? Interview residents on respiratory health impacts.
Developer angle: Are active ULURP projects (58-62 E. 125th St rezoning) or 434 DOB permits driving tree removal?

themes_detail.label: Residential Waste Management Spike
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked to 8 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a 0.5 weekly average—a 1500% increase (z-score: 8.66). Combined with graffiti complaints up 700% last week and the Community Board's persistent request for increased graffiti removal funding, this signals a sanitation and neighborhood maintenance crisis.
evidence: 8 residential disposal complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66)
3 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Community Board has repeated budget requests for 'Increase Graffiti Removal/Cleaning' (DSNY agency)—indicates chronic underfunding
reporting_angles: Is Sanitation Department adequately staffed in East Harlem? Interview DSNY about collection schedules and complaints.
Neighborhood quality-of-life story: How are residents coping with waste and graffiti accumulation?

themes_detail.label: Facility Maintenance Degradation
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints surged to 14 THREE WEEKS AGO versus a 3.5 weekly average—a 300% increase (z-score: 5.42). This suggests public infrastructure (parks, municipal facilities, or buildings) is deteriorating, aligning with Community Board requests for park and building improvements.
evidence: 14 maintenance/facility complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 3.5 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Community Board budget requests include 'Other requests for park, building, or access improvements' (DOT) and 'Other capital budget requests' (DEP)—repeated, unmet needs
reporting_angles: Which public facilities are deteriorating? Parks, schools, or municipal buildings? Conduct inventory.
Budget angle: Why are Community Board requests for facility improvements chronically unfunded?

themes_detail.label: Heat & Housing Crisis Baseline
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints remain the dominant 311 complaint category in East Harlem with 4,111 complaints over 90 days, far exceeding all other categories. While this is not a recent spike, it reflects a chronic housing crisis that warrants sustained coverage alongside acute emerging issues.
evidence: 4,111 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days—45.8% of total complaint volume; consistent year-over-year pattern
Residential noise complaints (2,302) and unsanitary conditions (811) suggest linked habitability issues in the same buildings
reporting_angles: Winter season story: Which landlords are chronic heat violators? Cross-reference 311 data with DOB complaints and court records.
Policy angle: Are HPD enforcement actions keeping pace with complaint volume?
